record.context_brief: recoverable sets in Gabor phase retrieval
record.original_question: In the Gaussian-window setting for Gabor phase retrieval from lattice samples, is there a dense set of functions in L^2(R) beyond the known examples that can be recovered up to global phase from their sampled Gabor magnitudes, and if so is that set meagre or comeagre in the sense of Baire category?

evidence.quote: Question 8.8. A more tractable problem than considering the recovery of all f P L2(R) up to a global phase using some window function w might be to instead focus on related problems in the Gabor setting. For instance, there is a dense set of functions in L2(R) that cannot be recovered up to a global phase from |Gf|2_aZ×bZ while the Gaussian w can be recovered up to a global phase from |Gw|2_aZ×bZ [3]. Is there a dense set of other functions that can also be recovered up to a global phase from Gabor magnitude measurements on Ω = aZ × bZ? If so, is this set of the first or second category?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G f(x,\omega) = \int_{\mathbb{R}} f(t)\, \overline{w(t-x)}\, e^{-2\pi i \omega t}\, dt$ denote the Gabor transform of $f \in L^2(\mathbb{R})$ with window $w$, and take $w(t) = e^{-\pi t^2}$ to be the standard Gaussian. Fix lattice parameters $a, b > 0$ and let $\Omega = a\mathbb{Z} \times b\mathbb{Z} \subset \mathbb{R}^2$. Two functions $f, g \in L^2(\mathbb{R})$ are said to be equal up to a global phase if there exists $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}$ with $g = e^{i\alpha} f$. Define
$$ \mathcal{R}_\Omega = \{\, f \in L^2(\mathbb{R}) : \text{if } g \in L^2(\mathbb{R}) \text{ satisfies } |Gg(x,\omega)| = |Gf(x,\omega)| \text{ for all } (x,\omega) \in \Omega, \text{ then } g = e^{i\alpha} f \text{ for some } \alpha \in \mathbb{R}\,\}, $$
the set of $L^2(\mathbb{R})$ functions that can be recovered up to a global phase from the sampled Gabor magnitudes on $\Omega$. It is known that the Gaussian itself lies in $\mathcal{R}_\Omega$ while there is a dense subset of $L^2(\mathbb{R})$ disjoint from $\mathcal{R}_\Omega$.

Determine whether $\mathcal{R}_\Omega$ contains a dense subset of $L^2(\mathbb{R})$ beyond the currently known examples, and if so decide whether $\mathcal{R}_\Omega$ is of the first category (meagre) or of the second category (comeagre) in $L^2(\mathbb{R})$ in the sense of Baire.
artifact.status_search_result: A 2025 preprint ("On a dense set of functions determined by sampled Gabor magnitude", arXiv:2507.14556) establishes that phase retrieval from sampled Gabor magnitudes is possible for a dense class of signals (those whose Bargmann transforms are entire functions of exponential type, sampled on uniformly discrete sets of sufficient lower Beurling density), thereby answering the existence part affirmatively for a broad class. However, this work does not appear to settle the Baire category (meagre vs. comeagre) question for the recoverable set in $L^2(\mathbb{R})$. The full question therefore appears only partially resolved.

status_evidence.title: On a dense set of functions determined by sampled Gabor magnitude
status_evidence.snippet: Phase retrieval is possible for a dense class of signals whose Bargmann transforms are entire functions of exponential type, recoverable from magnitude-only data on uniformly discrete sets of sufficient lower Beurling density.
status_evidence.claim: A dense set of recoverable functions beyond the Gaussian has been identified, but the Baire-category status of the recoverable set is not addressed.

status_evidence.title: Phase Retrieval from Sampled Gabor Transform Magnitudes: Counterexamples
status_evidence.snippet: For any lattice one can construct L^2(R) functions that do not agree up to global phase but whose sampled Gabor magnitudes coincide.
status_evidence.claim: There is a dense set of L^2(R) functions that cannot be recovered up to global phase from lattice Gabor magnitudes, motivating the question.

status_evidence.title: Injectivity of Gabor phase retrieval from lattice measurements
status_evidence.snippet: Studies which classes of functions are uniquely determined (up to global phase) by Gabor transform magnitudes on lattices.
status_evidence.claim: Provides positive recovery results for specific subclasses, supporting partial progress on the question.
